text: This little metal snail can make an engine way stronger. And it runs on the engine's own exhaust.
Hot exhaust blasts through the turbine side and spins the turbine wheel.
A shared shaft connects it to the compressor wheel. Same shaft, same spin.
The compressor crams fresh air into the engine at higher pressure. That extra pressure is called boost.
But squeezing air heats it up, and hot air is less dense. So it goes through an intercooler first.
Cooler, denser air means more air packed into every cylinder.
More air lets the engine burn more fuel. More fuel, more power.
It's not free power, though. Some of the engine's output goes into driving the turbo.
Exhaust in. Boost out. That's a turbo.
